svg.text: Selection moved the trained value only when candidates disagreed within a prompt
Both arms were offered candidate pools with the identical mean risk value every round — largest difference between
arms 0.000 across all 11 rounds. They differed only in where the variation sat.
One model family throughout — Qwen3-4B with a risk-seeking persona installed by fine-tuning. Selection is an oracle that keeps the
highest-risk answers, not a language-model judge. Each round: 12 gamble prompts, 12 candidate answers generated per prompt, 6
offered to the selector, 2 kept and LoRA fine-tuned on. Value is the share of answers choosing the gamble, measured on 12 held-out
gamble prompts at 12 samples each.
The value climbs only in the spread arm
each line is one training loop: two independent runs x two seeds

One of the four loops stops after round 2: in that round the concentrated arm's
candidates were so value-uniform that no offered-pool mean was reachable by both
arms, so the run was ended rather than let the arms differ.
Why: a value-uniform prompt has nothing to select on

Source: experiments/spread_intervention/output_oracle/spread_intervention.json (run 1) and experiments/spread_intervention/output_followups/floor_effect.json (run 2),
groups whose names begin with oracle_max. The two runs installed the risk persona at different strengths, which is why their round-0 values differ.
